lines.en: That's us in front of the fireplace, with my grandfather and all the cousins.
lines.pt: Somos nós na frente da lareira, com meu avô e todos os primos.

lines.en: When I was a child, we used to sing carols every December on the porch.
lines.pt: Quando eu era criança, a gente costumava cantar cantigas de Natal todo dezembro na varanda.

lines.en: Really? We sang too, but only after dinner. My dad played the guitar, badly.
lines.pt: Sério? A gente cantava também, mas só depois do jantar. Meu pai tocava violão, mal.

lines.en: That sounds lovely. Did you use to stay up late on Christmas Eve? I never could, because my parents checked on me every hour.
lines.pt: Que lindo. Você costumava ficar acordada até tarde na véspera de Natal? Eu nunca conseguia, porque meus pais me vigiavam toda hora.

lines.en: Never! Mom didn't use to let us open anything before breakfast, not even a small gift.
lines.pt: Nunca! A mamãe não deixava a gente abrir nada antes do café da manhã, nem um presente pequeno.

lines.en: Poor you! We always picked the biggest box, of course.
lines.pt: Coitada! Claro que sempre escolhíamos a caixa maior.

lines.en: Ha! My grandfather read us a story every night instead.
lines.pt: Ha! Meu avô lia uma história para nós toda noite.

lines.en: That's sweet. We left milk and cookies for Santa, and my brother ate them himself before sunrise.
lines.pt: Que fofo. A gente deixava leite e biscoitos para o Papai Noel, e meu irmão comia tudo antes do nascer do sol.

lines.en: No way! Did your parents ever catch him? I'd have loved to see their faces when they found the empty plate.
lines.pt: Não acredito! Seus pais nunca o pegaram? Eu adoraria ter visto a cara deles ao achar o prato vazio.

lines.en: Never. He blamed the dog every year, and nobody ever doubted him.
lines.pt: Nunca. Ele botava a culpa no cachorro todo ano e ninguém nunca duvidou.

lines.en: Classic! Hold on, let me get my camera.
lines.pt: Clássico! Espere, vou pegar minha câmera.

facts.big: When I was a child, we used to sing
facts.label: Used to
facts.sub: Use used to + verbo para hábitos do passado. Na pergunta e na negativa: use to.

facts.label: costumava + verbo
facts.sub: Use used to para falar de hábitos do passado que acabaram: We used to sing carols. She used to wait with a camera. O verbo fica na forma base.

facts.label: Você costumava…?
facts.sub: Na pergunta, use did + use to: Did you use to stay up late? Did your mother use to be angry? Não use used com did.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “a gente costumava cantar” e “eu não costumava dormir cedo”.
compare.us: Em inglês, use used to + verbo para hábitos do passado que já acabaram: We used to sing. Na pergunta e na negativa, use use to: Did you use to…? I didn’t use to…

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We used to sing carols means we sang them often in the past.
We say “Did you used to stay up late?”
items.why: In questions, we say use to: Did you use to stay up late?

items.s: Used to can talk about a past habit that is finished.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We used to sing carols means we sang them often in the past. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “Did you used to stay up late?” → Falso (In questions, we say use to: Did you use to stay up late?)
Used to can talk about a past habit that is finished. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Christmas memories in Dallas · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cold December evening in Dallas. Dora’s living room is full of lights. Leo sits on the sofa with a cup of tea. A small tree stands near the window. Old songs play on the radio. The two friends start to remember.

“When I was a child, we used to sing carols every night in December.” says Dora. “Really? We used to open one small gift every night.” says Leo. “My grandfather used to read us a story by the fireplace.” says Dora.

pages.title: Christmas memories in Dallas · 3/3
paragraphs: “When I was little, we used to leave milk and cookies for Santa Claus.” says Leo. “We did that too! I miss those days, but I still sing the same songs.” says Dora. Dora finds an old photo in a box. Leo laughs when he sees the tree. They sing one carol together. Dora says the best gift was the time together. Leo agrees and finishes his tea. Good memories make the room feel warm.
